T1.implementation_approach: Create a user-friendly interface with search, filter, and sorting options for problems.
T1.notes: Ensure responsive design for various devices.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle problem data retrieval, creation, and updates.

T3.implementation_approach: Set up a relational database schema to store problem details, tags, and metadata.

T4.implementation_approach: Design an intuitive UI for users to submit code and view submission results.
T4.notes: Include real-time feedback for submission status.

T5.implementation_approach: Implement logic to compile, execute, and evaluate code submissions against test cases.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a profile page to display user details, achievements, and activity history.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to manage user data, authentication, and profile updates.

T8.implementation_approach: Set up a database schema to store user profiles, preferences, and activity logs.

T9.implementation_approach: Create a leaderboard UI to display rankings based on user performance metrics.
T9.notes: Include filters for different criteria like time period or problem category.

T10.implementation_approach: Develop backend logic to calculate and update leaderboard rankings dynamically.

T11.implementation_approach: Design a UI to display hints and tutorials in an organized and accessible manner.
T11.notes: Include search functionality for easy navigation.

T12.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and tutorials content, including retrieval and updates.

T13.implementation_approach: Set up a database schema to store hints, tutorials, and associated metadata.

T14.implementation_approach: Perform UI testing to ensure responsiveness, usability, and cross-browser compatibility.
T14.notes: Use automated tools like Selenium for efficiency.

T15.implementation_approach: Test backend APIs for functionality, performance, and security using tools like Postman.

T16.implementation_approach: Validate database schema, queries, and data integrity through unit and integration tests.
T16.notes: Test for edge cases and large datasets.

T17.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform on a cloud service with CI/CD pipelines for automated updates.
T17.notes: Ensure proper monitoring and logging post-deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize the SQLAlchemy instance
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.id} - {self.title}>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), nullable=False, unique=True)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), nullable=False, unique=True)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    # Relationships
    problems = db.relationship('Problem', backref='user', lazy=True)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

    def to_dict(self):
        """Return a dictionary representation of the user."""
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'username': self.username,
            'email': self.email,
            'created_at': self.created_at,
            'updated_at': self.updated_at
        }

from app.database import db
from app.models.problem import Problem
from app.models.user import User

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    status = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False, default='pending')  # e.g., 'pending', 'accepted', 'rejected'
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Solution id={self.id} user_id={self.user_id} problem_id={self.problem_id} status={self.status}>"

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'user_id': self.user_id,
            'problem_id': self.problem_id,
            'code': self.code,
            'status': self.status,
            'created_at': self.created_at,
            'updated_at': self.updated_at
        }

from flask import Blueprint, request, jsonify
from app.database import db
from app.models.solution import Solution
from app.models.problem import Problem
from app.models.user import User

solution_bp = Blueprint('solution', __name__)

@solution_bp.route('/solutions', methods=['GET'])
def get_solutions():
    """
    Retrieve all solutions from the database.
    """
    solutions = Solution.query.all()
    return jsonify([solution.to_dict() for solution in solutions]), 200

@solution_bp.route('/solutions/<int:solution_id>', methods=['GET'])
def get_solution(solution_id):
    """
    Retrieve a specific solution by its ID.
    """
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if solution:
        return jsonify(solution.to_dict()), 200
    return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404

@solution_bp.route('/solutions', methods=['POST'])
def create_solution():
    """
    Create a new solution.
    Request JSON should contain: user_id, problem_id, code, status.
    """
    data = request.get_json()

    # Validate necessary fields
    required_fields = ['user_id', 'problem_id', 'code', 'status']
    if not all(field in data for field in required_fields):
        return jsonify({'error': 'Missing required fields'}), 400

    # Validate user and problem existence
    user = User.query.get(data['user_id'])
    problem = Problem.query.get(data['problem_id'])
    if not user or not problem:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid user_id or problem_id'}), 400

    # Create and save the solution
    new_solution = Solution(
        user_id=data['user_id'],
        problem_id=data['problem_id'],
        code=data['code'],
        status=data['status']
    )
    db.session.add(new_solution)
    db.session.commit()

    return jsonify(new_solution.to_dict()), 201

@solution_bp.route('/solutions/<int:solution_id>', methods=['PUT'])
def update_solution(solution_id):
    """
    Update an existing solution.
    Request JSON can contain: code, status.
    """
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if not solution:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404

    data = request.get_json()
    if 'code' in data:
        solution.code = data['code']
    if 'status' in data:
        solution.status = data['status']

    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify(solution.to_dict()), 200

@solution_bp.route('/solutions/<int:solution_id>', methods=['DELETE'])
def delete_solution(solution_id):
    """
    Delete a solution by its ID.
    """
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if not solution:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404

    db.session.delete(solution)
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify({'message': 'Solution deleted successfully'}), 200

    # Register routes and blueprints

    # Define home route
    @app.route('/')
    def home():
        return render_template('index.html')

    return app

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Repository: A comprehensive collection of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive automated feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Enables users to create profiles to track their progress, achievements, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Tutorials: Provides hints and tutorials for solving problems to help users improve their skills.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
